The test image shows corn kernels (seed/ear) with white cottony mycelium growing between and on the kernels, which appear tan/brownish and discolored. This points to an ear rot disease.

Top candidates: Fusarium_Disease (whitish to pink growth), Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mycelium from base), Gibberella_Disease (pink/red at tip).

Let me check one reference image for Fusarium_Disease.

The reference Fusarium image shows white to pinkish mold on scattered kernels. The test image shows kernels with a glassy/translucent tan appearance and prominent white mycelium between kernels — consistent with heavy Fusarium infection. The coloration (white-pinkish mycelium, tan/discolored kernels) fits Fusarium better than Diplodia (which produces more grayish-brown mummified kernels) or Gibberella (which shows distinctly red/pink mold at ear tip).
